quickAnswer: Belek is a purpose-built luxury golf and all-inclusive enclave 35 minutes east of Antalya Airport. It excels for serious golfers, multi-generational families wanting effortless kids' clubs, and winter-sun travellers, but disappoints boutique travellers seeking historic streets, local neighbourhood restaurants, or independent harbour towns.

body.text: Most online coverage of belek luxury resorts reads like hotel press copy because booking portals earn heavy commissions on five-star all-inclusive stays. Here is the straight assessment: Belek executes large-scale resort hospitality better than almost anywhere in the Mediterranean, yet it is also a gated tourism bubble with almost no historic town centre. Knowing which side of that trade-off fits your trip saves you from booking the wrong coast.
Who is Belek best suited for vs boutique travellers?

Belek is ideal for golfers, families travelling with children or grandparents, and winter travellers wanting heated pools, high-spec spas, and predictable service under one roof. Boutique travellers who want to wander stone lanes, choose a different neighbourhood meyhane each night, and feel rooted in local Turkish town life should pick Kaleiçi, Kaş, or Bozburun instead.

The contrast is structural, not accidental. Belek was master-planned in the late 1980s and 1990s along a flat, pine-backed sandy coastline specifically for large-footprint resorts and championship fairways. Inside top-tier properties such as Maxx Royal Belek, Regnum Carya, Cullinan Belek, or Gloria Serenity, standards are genuinely high: à la carte restaurants, imported spirits, heated outdoor winter pools, and professional kids' academies operate smoothly.

Step outside the resort gates, however, and Belek town is a compact commercial strip of golf-gear shops, pharmacies, and souvenir stalls. If your idea of a good evening is stumbling onto a family-run harbour table, Belek will feel sterile by day three.

body.text: Which Belek golf courses are open year-round?

All major Belek championship courses remain open 12 months a year, thanks to mild Mediterranean winters and Bermuda/overseeded ryegrass fairways. Standout year-round clubs include Carya Golf Club (with 18 floodlit holes), Montgomerie Maxx Royal, Cornelia Golf Club's 27-hole Faldo layout, Gloria Golf Club's 45 holes, and Cullinan Links.

Belek's prime golf window actually runs from October through May, when northern European courses are waterlogged and Belek sits between 15°C and 25°C. A few practical distinctions matter when choosing a club:

items: [Carya Golf Club](https://www.caryagolf.com/en/golf/floodlight/): Europe's first course with all 18 holes under floodlights, allowing evening rounds in summer heat or after-dark winter play; requires a 36 handicap limit.

[Montgomerie Maxx Royal](https://www.maxxroyal.com/maxx-royal-belek/golf): Colin Montgomerie design and former Turkish Airlines Open host, with floodlighting across the final nine holes and an all-inclusive clubhouse for players.

[Cornelia Golf Club](https://www.corneliaresort.com/EN/Cornelia-Golf-Club): Three interchangeable nine-hole loops (King, Queen, Prince) designed by Sir Nick Faldo, walkable from Cornelia Diamond and Azure Villas.
Overseeding alert: Most Belek courses close briefly (usually 10 to 14 days in late September or early October) for annual autumn overseeding—verify maintenance dates before locking in flights.

body.text: How far is Belek from Antalya Airport and Kaleiçi?

Belek sits 30 to 35 kilometres east of [Antalya Airport (AYT)](https://www.antalya-airport.aero/homepage), taking 30 to 45 minutes by private transfer depending on your exact resort zone (Kadriye is closer; Boğazkent adds 10 minutes). Central Antalya and historic Kaleiçi lie 42 kilometres west, roughly 45 to 55 minutes by car outside peak rush hour.

There is no direct municipal tram or airport bus into Belek's resort strip—public transit requires changing at Serik or Aksu and takes over two hours. Book a fixed-price private transfer in advance (typically €45–€65 per vehicle from AYT) rather than negotiating at the taxi rank. For a broader look at southern airport logistics, read our [Dalaman vs Antalya Airport comparison](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/dalaman-vs-antalya-airport).
Can you mix a Belek resort stay with private cultural day trips?

Yes—and for many families or mixed-interest couples, combining three to four nights in Belek with two private cultural outings works remarkably well. Because Belek sits right on the Pamphylian plain, you reach Aspendos in 25 minutes, Perge in 30 minutes, and Side in 45 minutes without enduring long highway transfers.

This split solves a common household compromise: one partner plays morning golf or relaxes by the pool while the other joins—or the whole family takes a half-day private car with a licensed archaeologist guide to [Aspendos Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=ASP01&DistId=ASP) and [Perge Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=PRG01&DistId=PRG) before returning for a late lunch. You can even pair Belek with a half-day mountain hike at Termessos (75 minutes away). See our [Aspendos, Perge and Side route guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/aspendos-perge-side) for exact timing.

faq.q: Are Belek's luxury all-inclusive resorts worth the high nightly rate?
faq.a: They deliver strong value if you actively use the golf courses, heated pools, kids' clubs, and à la carte dining. If you plan to eat out every night and spend most days touring off-property, you are paying for resort inclusions you will barely touch.

faq.q: Which Belek resorts are best in winter (November to March)?
faq.a: Maxx Royal Belek, Regnum Carya, Cullinan Belek, and Gloria Serenity stay open year-round with heated outdoor pools, full indoor spas, and reduced winter rates, though beachfront piers and some summer-only restaurants close between November and March.

faq.q: Do you need to stay at a golf resort to play Belek's courses?
faq.a: No. Non-resident golfers can book tee times at Carya, Montgomerie, Cornelia, Gloria, and National, though hotel guests typically receive preferential green fees and earlier tee-time priority during peak October–November and March–April golf weeks.

faq.q: Is the beach in Belek sandy or pebbly?
faq.a: Belek has a wide, flat, coarse-sand beach with gentle entry into the Mediterranean, plus private resort piers with sunbeds. Unlike rocky coves in Kaş or Bozburun, the water here is open-sea and can get choppy on windy afternoons.

faq.q: How far is Belek from The Land of Legends theme park?
faq.a: The Land of Legends sits right inside the Kadriye zone of Belek—between 5 and 15 minutes by car from most Belek resorts. Several nearby properties, including Rixos hotels, include complimentary entry and shuttle transfers.

faq.q: Should you rent a car when staying in Belek?
faq.a: Not for a pure resort-and-golf week, as clubs provide transfers between resorts and fairways. If you plan three or more independent day trips to Perge, Aspendos, Side, Kaleiçi, or Termessos, either rent a car for those days or book a private driver.
